LESSON: ACIDS, BASES AND INDICATORS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 2.2: Acids, bases and indicators
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 22

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Acids, bases and indicators, part of Mixtures, Elements and Compounds in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why are acids and bases important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Use litmus paper to classify household solutions into acids and bases. Safety precautions should be taken

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Use litmus paper to classify household solutions into acids and bases. Safety precautions should be taken

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Acids, bases and indicators together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner acquires data recording and presentation techniques as carry out

activities to investigate the physical properties of acids and bases.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner develops research skills as they explore applications of acids and

16

bases using print or digital media.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner acquires innovative practices as they use acid-base indicator from plant extracts

to classify common household solutions as either acidic or basic.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner engages in assigned roles as they carry out activities to prepare acid-base indicators from

plant extracts collaboratively.

• Respect: The learner works with peers and recognises each other’s contribution(s) as they prepare acid-base indicators

from plant extracts, and dispose of laboratory waste responsibly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: The learner learn how to use flowers sparingly to protect plants as they use acid-base indicator

from plant extracts to classify common household solutions as either acidic or basic.

Link to other learning area:

The learner is able to relate the content of acids and bases is to testing soil acidity and application of lime and fertilizers to

improve soil fertility and pH in agriculture and nutrition.
